thread:
eva: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak (PR #4567) I'm seeing a host-side p99 jump on small-chat workloads.
sam: ugh, saw that in dashboards too. p50 steady, p99 went from ~12ms -> ~28ms for decode+ingress. any obvious traces?
miguel: I grabbed a flamegraph from the canary host: https://perf.company/fg/2298765432 (sampled, 10s). It shows tokenization and gRPC writev coalescing as hot spots.
jin: paste of the top stacks:
```
main.decode_token -> tokenizer.tokenize -> net.writev -> http2.session.write -> kernel_selector.choose
```
The tokenization moved earlier in the pipeline with the PR; maybe we lost batching opportunities for writev.
eva: exact numbers from the trace: tokenization ~35% CPU, writev/http2 ~22%, kernel selection ~10%. kvcache miss rate stayed flat at 4.2% so probably not cache-related.
sam: interesting — kernel_selector now biases towards "fast-kernel" for short sequences, which increased kernel churn. that could increase syscalls if it reduces coalescing windows.
miguel: also noticed an increase in smallwrites ratio (requests with <512B payload) from 18% -> 32% on canary. that aligns with writev impact.
pryce: should we roll back the selector change? or try a quick mitigation: introduce a micro-coalesce layer that waits up to 2ms for additional small frames before flushing.
jin: can we simulate the micro-coalesce locally? I sketched a small patch to sidecar preparse: add a 500-2000us batching window for writev. microbench shows p99 drops back to ~14ms on emulator.
eva: snippet of the bench command I ran:
```
./bench-host --qps 400 --payload-dist small --trace out.json
jq '.p99' out.json
```
sam: nice. But 2ms delay might violate our 99.5% SLO for <50ms interactive flows. maybe adaptive: only coalesce if the request is <1KB and current outstanding QPS < X.
miguel: another idea: avoid re-tokenizing identical prefixes by moving prefix tokenization into the ingress cache (prefixKVC). we could hash first 64 bytes and consult prefix cache before tokenizing.
jin: prefix cache would cut tokenization CPU but adds lookup overhead — it's a net win if hit rate > ~10% on small-chat. current requests show ~12% identical prefixes in production logs for some customers.
eva: also found increased HPACK overhead on the HTTP/2 control path: repeated small header frames increased CPU in http2.compress. That plus more small payloads amplifies CPU.
pryce: action items I suggest:
- revert kernel-selector bias (short-term rollback) (owner: sam) :thumbsup:
- prototype micro-coalesce with 0.5/2ms adaptive window (owner: jin)
- run prefix tokenization cache experiment (owner: miguel)
- add telemetry for smallwrite ratio per route (owner: eva)
I'll open a short-lived RFC and link PRs.
deploy-bot: canary deploy 2298765432 -> 2298765432-rc2 rolled to 3 hosts at 2026-03-23T09:12:00Z
sam: i'll slot the rollback today if we don't see better signals from jin's patch in the next 2 hours.
jin: pushing a canary PR now: https://git.company/p/redwood/runtime/pulls/4590 — includes micro-coalesce behind a flag and heuristics.
miguel: i'll prepare a replay test using live logs to estimate prefix cache hit rate per-customer.
eva: thanks all. I'll update the dashboards to show p50/p95/p99 for decode+ingress and smallwrite ratio by route.
sam: if jin's fixes look promising we can avoid rollback. else rollback at 11:30 PT.
eva: tagging oncall — @pryce please watch infra alerts for increased latency while we test.
pryce: watching. will post if any CPU storms or node restarts show up.
